title: Governed change, mutation, effects, and recovery
problem: Consequential candidate selection, concurrent mutation, ambiguous external outcomes, and recovery can lose impact, authority, idempotency, or residual-consequence semantics when represented as generic success or failure.
invariant: A triggered change records its exact subject and base, impact, separately valid authority, effect boundary, evidence, and truthful terminal or unresolved disposition; action selection is not authorization, acknowledgement is not truth, and compensation is not rollback.
applicability_triggers: A resolver can propose materially different consequential outcomes.
Concurrent writers can mutate the same authoritative state.
A consequential external effect can be duplicated, partially applied, or ambiguously acknowledged.
Durable partial work requires typed retry, reconciliation, compensation, restore, abandon, or escalation.
non_applicability_triggers: The operation is a reversible repository-local edit already governed by existing task and Git contracts.
There is no external effect, competing authoritative writer, or durable partial outcome.
exclusions: No universal action or lifecycle enum.
No provider, product, workflow, or topology vocabulary.
No outbox, distributed transaction, idempotency service, or external-effect runtime.
No inference that a selected action is permitted.
required_contracts: Impact module: exact subject/base, dependencies, affected scope, uncertainty, validation, and rollback or compensation posture.
Action module: project-owned variants including explicit no-op, decline, defer, and unresolved outcomes.
Mutation-effect module: mutation owner, fence/base, authorization reference, idempotency identity, boundary, receipt, read-back, and unknown outcome.
Recovery-incident module: failure class, point of no return, retry/reconcile/compensate/restore/abandon/escalate choice, residual consequences, and terminal disposition.
prohibited_shortcuts: Blind retry after an ambiguous consequential effect.
Treating external acknowledgement as authoritative outcome.
Building generic distributed-systems machinery without an exact adopter boundary.
failure_recovery_semantics: Unknown external outcome remains explicit until safe read-back or reconciliation resolves it.
Irreversible effects retain residual consequences and cannot claim rollback.
Recovery preserves unaffected work and requires current authority for any new effect.
proof_expectations: Supply an exact adopter, authoritative owner, transaction/effect boundary, and failure model.
Exercise stale base, changed dependency, unauthorized effect, duplicate delivery, crash boundaries, timeout/read-back, revocation, unknown outcome, and compensation.
Demonstrate that unrelated work remains safe and incident reconstruction is complete.
known_implementations: Octon Mini transactional generation, refresh, migrations, typed Git operations, concurrency modifier, and operations recovery are partial specialized realizations.

evidence.exact_subject: Project Blueprint 3.0.0 local mutation, Git operation, migration, and recovery contracts
evidence.supports: Specialized local mechanisms demonstrate the invariant while a generic external-effect protocol remains unjustified.
limitations: No concrete external-effect adopter or provider boundary has been proven.

compatibility.migration_posture: Catalog admission only; existing tasks, Git workflows, operations records, and generated projects are unchanged.

migration.guidance: Catalog admission changes no task, Git, operations, or effect record. A later implemented package requires its own migration decision.

complexity: A future adopter may require variants, impact records, concurrency control, receipts, reconciliation, and operational procedures.
operator_burden: Failure handling and effect reconciliation require project-specific ownership and exercises.

status_history.rationale: Allocated for explicit architecture review without implementation.
Admitted as four independently triggered optional modules; implementation awaits a concrete adopter.

limitations: Catalog admission does not authorize schemas, runtime machinery, generated files, or profile defaults.
Each module remains separately trigger-gated and project-specialized.
